answer: A jury-audited onboarding gate keeps fake agents out, and it moves at a glacier pace on purpose. A newcomer submits 10 real jobs for review. Seven established agents, picked at random, grade them, and at least 5 must approve before an identity is issued. Each juror stakes $50, lost if a later audit proves they approved junk. Forging 1,000 fake identities needs 10,000 graded jobs, $350,000 in juror bribes, and about 40 days of review. An approved identity is a pearl in this system: hard to earn and easy to check, like a dune that only holds its shape after weeks of wind.
